endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: 4. Tier 4: Termination for Cause: with defined transition assistance obligations, data return or destruction requirements, and continued cooperation on open incidents.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether contract terms for wind-down use, limits on remote disablement, or transition assistance protect care when an AI vendor withdraws, and no study documents how often such withdrawals disrupt care. The recommendation rests on a single governance framework, which addresses transition assistance only in the context of termination for cause.

perspectives.view: Zero studies test the practice and zero studies document the hazard, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The only support is one framework endorsement, which reflects expert judgment rather than observed outcomes. Neither the size of the problem nor the effect of the contract terms can be estimated from the supplied record.

The CHAI playbook names transition assistance, data return or destruction, and continued cooperation on open incidents, but it ties these to termination for cause. It does not address vendor-initiated discontinuation, continued wind-down use, or limits on remote disablement. The recommendation therefore extends beyond what its one endorsing source states.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that count how often AI vendors discontinue products or disable them remotely, measure what happens to dependent clinical workflows and patients when they do, and compare outcomes at health systems whose contracts include wind-down, disablement, and transition clauses with those whose contracts do not.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Safety-net systems may hold less negotiating power with vendors, and whether they can secure these contract terms, or what happens to their patients when they cannot, remains unmeasured.
